newsitem.title: USA: Defense bill advances, exceeds Clinton request.
newsitem.headline: Defense bill advances, exceeds Clinton request.

text.p: House-Senate negotiators approved a near $245 billion defence appropriation bill Thursday that they said was $9.4 billion more than President Clinton requested.
They predicted Clinton would accept the bill despite earlier threats to veto the huge increase.

Negotiators said Defence Secretary William Perry told them two weeks ago he could recommend approval of about a $9 billion increase, though they said the administration has not said specifically that it would accept the bill negotiators approved Thursday.
Even so, Sen. Ted Stevens, an Alaska Republican, and House Appropriations Committee Chairman Bob Livingston, a Louisiana Republican, used the same words: "The president will not veto this bill."

Defence bills approved by the House and Senate this year have all exceeded Clinton's request by at least $10 billion and the White House has threatened to veto them all on grounds that domestic programmes need the extra money.

The bill includes $325 million more than Clinton requested for anti-missile defence research to speed up construction of such a defence for U.S. cities. A separate bill would order construction of the defence by the year 2003.
-- A three percent military pay raise and $600 million more than Clinton requested to improve deteriorating military housing.

-- $500 million more than Clinton requested for ships, including an additional roll-on-roll-off heavy combat weapons ship for the Army and two additional ships for the Marines outfitted with combat weapons to move quickly into war.

-- $650 million Clinton requested for a third Seawolf submarine to be built by General Dynamics Electric Boat in Groton, Connecticut, plus $296 million for the first of a new class of attack submarines to be built by Electric Boat, and $500 million for a second of the submarines to be built by Newport News, Va., Shipbuilding and Drydock Co.

-- Six more Navy F/A-18 fighter bombers than Clinton asked for, to be built by McDonnell Douglas Corp.; two more Air Force F-15 fighters by McDonnell Douglas and two more Air Force F-16 fighters built by Lockheed Martin.
